description: One-factor-at-a-time study of prompt, specification, test feedback/provision, implementation substrate, scaffold, and reference access for the PiCC construction task.

provenance.creator: study-author
provenance.source: PiCC task contract and Writing a C Compiler test-suite scope

conditions.description: Behavioral specification in TASK.md, detailed workflow prompt, failure-level test tool, empty Rust repository, and no reference implementation.

Remove workflow, progress-memory, sequencing, and regression-management instructions from every prompt surface while retaining safety and task rules. The initial and continuation requests are also stripped; leaving the shared ones in place re-supplied the removed instructions each round.
Replace the detailed behavioral specification with a concise product brief of the same feature scope.
Provide the full baseline behavioral specification plus prescribed lexer/parser/sema/IR/codegen boundaries and invariants. Differs from baseline only by the added architecture sections.

provenance.creator: study-author
provenance.source: Behavioral scope plus conventional compiler architecture guidance

conditions.description: Provide the same behavioral specification in the initial request rather than as a persistent TASK.md file.
Withhold visible tests and all visible scores while retaining post-hoc hidden evaluation.
Expose only aggregate visible score/build status, withholding per-stage and per-test failures.
Expose the same visible test corpus as readable source files while retaining baseline failure-level evaluator feedback.
Expose a deterministic, family-grouped 25% subset of the baseline visible tests.
Use Python 3 and the standard library rather than Rust, with the same external compiler contract and tests.
Start from a buildable Rust lexer/parser/sema/IR/codegen scaffold instead of an empty repository.
Provide a rate-limited black-box reference behavior oracle while withholding source code.
